water-engineering.lead: Bulk water is the largest part of what Unicon does and has been since the mid-nineties. Reservoirs, treatment works, pump stations and pipelines — the structures that have to hold, and keep holding, for fifty years.
intro: A water-retaining structure is unforgiving in a way an office block is not. It either holds or it does not, the defect shows up years after the contractor has left, and the repair costs more than the original pour. That is why our teams are built around concrete discipline rather than programme heroics: mix design, placement, curing, joint detailing and testing are the whole job.

We work as a principal contractor to consulting engineers across KwaZulu-Natal and the Eastern Cape, most often under the GCC suite for municipal and water board clients. Our people have poured circular and rectangular reservoirs, post-tensioned walls, dome roofs, contact tanks, clarifiers, filter beds and every chamber in between.

water-engineering.method_heading: How A Reservoir Actually Gets Built.

method.d: Access, laydown, batching arrangements and survey control. On rural sites this includes water supply for the works itself, which is often the first thing we have to solve.
Excavation to founding level, inspection with the engineer, blinding and any founding improvement. Nothing is poured until the founding is signed off.
Base slab in panels with waterstops, then walls in lifts with purpose-made formwork. Mix design, placement rate, vibration and curing are controlled to the specification, not to the programme.
Tendon installation, stressing to the designed force with recorded elongations, and grouting. Stressing records form part of the handover pack.
Dome, flat or beam-and-slab roof, waterproofing, hatches, ladders, handrails, ventilation and level instrumentation.
Fill, stand and watertightness test against the specified drop, disinfection where potable, then wet commissioning with the client's operators present.

Excavators, TLBs, rollers and compaction plant
Mobile cranes and telehandlers for roof and plant installation
Pipe-laying, welding and pressure-testing equipment
Site laboratory arrangements and independent cube testing

civil-engineering.lead: Provincial bridges, river crossings, canals and mass earthworks. Work that gets built in a live river, under traffic, or in a season that will not wait.
intro: Heavy civils is the discipline where the site dictates the method. A river bridge is governed by the flood season, a road widening by the traffic accommodation, a canal by the irrigation calendar. Our long relationship with the KZN Department of Transport has been built on getting those constraints right before the first machine moves.

The scope runs from bulk earthworks and layerworks through to the finished deck: substructure, superstructure, approach works, guardrails and rehabilitation. We work almost entirely under the GCC suite, priced to SANS 1200 and constructed to the provincial standard specifications.

civil-engineering.method_heading: Building A Bridge In A Live River.

method.d: Substructure work in a river bed is scheduled into the low-flow window. Getting that wrong costs a season, so it is decided before tender price is confirmed.
Coffer dams, diversion channels and dewatering designed and signed off, with traffic accommodation in place before the road is touched.
Excavation to founding, inspection, then bases, piers, abutments and wing walls. Founding conditions in a river bed frequently differ from the borehole log, so early exposure matters.
Falsework or precast beams, deck reinforcement and pour, then parapets, joints, surfacing and drainage.
Approach fills, layerworks, guardrails, road furniture, then rehabilitation of the working area and river bed.

structural-engineering.lead: Reinforced and post-tensioned concrete, formwork engineering and the finishes that decide whether a structure lasts thirty years or thirteen.
intro: Most of what Unicon builds is concrete, and most of that concrete has to be watertight, load-bearing or both. Over thirty-five years the company has specialised in the harder end of that: circular post-tensioned walls, dome roofs, suspended decks and liquid-retaining structures where the specification allows almost no crack width.

Structural concrete is not a separate division so much as the discipline underneath the water, civils and building teams. The same supervisors, formwork systems and testing regime move between a reservoir, a bridge deck and a suspended slab in a shopping centre.

structural-engineering.method_heading: Why The Pour Is Planned Before It Is Poured.

method.d: Sequence, joint positions, placement rate, plant, standby plant and labour are agreed with the engineer in writing before the pour is booked.
Formwork alignment, tie positions, cover, joint preparation and waterstops are inspected and signed. This is the last moment anything can be fixed cheaply.
Continuous placement at the agreed rate with correct vibration, controlled lift heights and monitored temperature. A pour that stops halfway makes a joint nobody designed.
Curing starts immediately and runs for the specified period. On water-retaining work this is the single most common cause of defects elsewhere, and we treat it accordingly.
Strike to the agreed strength, inspect the finish, record the cube results and close out the pour in the quality file.

general-building.lead: Retail centres, schools, clinics, offices and homes. The company started with rural clinics and classrooms in 1991 and has kept a building team ever since.

Building work has stayed part of the business ever since, and it is the side of the company that runs under the JBCC suite rather than GCC — shopping centres, tertiary education facilities, medical suites, offices and private homes.

Because the same company also does the civils, a building contract that involves platform earthworks, bulk services, stormwater or a reservoir does not need a second contractor. That is usually where the programme is won or lost on a greenfield site.

agricultural-engineering.lead: Abattoirs, dairies, processing lines and farm infrastructure — built to the standards a regulator will actually inspect.
agricultural-engineering.evidence_note: Agricultural work is a specialised, smaller part of our record. The projects below are what the database shows, and they range from a high-throughput abattoir to farm infrastructure and irrigation canal work.
intro: A processing facility is not a shed. An abattoir is graded and inspected, a dairy has hygiene and effluent requirements written into its operating licence, and a facility that cannot pass inspection cannot trade. That turns an agricultural project into a compliance exercise as much as a construction one.

Unicon has delivered a high-throughput abattoir for a provincial department, dairy and farm infrastructure, a saw mill processing line and irrigation canal work. The common thread is a client who needs the facility to work operationally on day one, not just to be complete.

intro: Mines do not usually need a contractor to mine. They need someone who can build the water storage, the pipelines, the heavy foundations and the platforms that keep the operation running — and who will work to the mine's permit system without argument.

That is where Unicon fits. The 10ML post-tensioned reservoir with a dome roof at Thabazimbi for Anglo American is the same structure type we have built repeatedly for water boards and municipalities, delivered to a mining client's standards and audit regime.

renewable-energy.lead: Balance-of-plant civil works for generation projects: platforms, foundations, hardstands, access roads and site water.
renewable-energy.evidence_note: We have not yet delivered a renewable energy generation project, and we are not going to imply otherwise. What this page sets out is the civil scope on a solar, wind or biomass site and the comparable work behind it — mass earthworks, heavy foundations, access roads, hardstands and water infrastructure that Unicon has been building since 1991. If you are assembling a balance-of-plant package, judge us on that record rather than on a logo wall.
intro: On a renewable energy project the generation equipment comes from the technology supplier. What is left is a civil engineering contract: platform earthworks over a large footprint, several hundred foundations built to tight tolerance, access roads that carry abnormal loads, cable trenching, hardstands and the water infrastructure that keeps the site operating.

That work is not new to us, even though the application is. Mass earthworks, bridge and plant foundations, haul roads, hardstands and reservoirs are the daily business of the civils and water teams. The honest position is that we bring thirty-five years of heavy civil delivery to a sector we have not yet built in — which is why we would expect to be judged on the underlying work rather than on sector references we do not have.

renewable-energy.method_heading: How We Would Approach A Balance-Of-Plant Package.

method.d: Foundation quantities on a generation site are driven by ground conditions across a large footprint. We would want the geotechnical picture verified before the foundation method is fixed.
Several hundred near-identical foundations is a production problem. The gain is in the jig, the sequence and the survey control, not in working faster.
Access roads and hardstands are built to carry the heaviest delivery on the project, early, because everything else depends on them.
Tolerances, setting-out and handover of foundations are agreed with the equipment supplier in writing before the first pour.
Local labour and enterprise obligations are met with real packages and real support on site, which is how we already work on municipal contracts.
